title: Prior-auth bead 002 hangs when a concurrent tool call fails
description:
REPRODUCIBLE. In bead 002 (clinical review + coverage, ConcurrentBuilder), the workflow hangs indefinitely at ~95% CPU with no further log output whenever an MCP tool raises.

Root cause (isolated 2026-07-31): the stage issues six tool calls. The four coverage tools return normally. The two hybrid_search calls FAIL server-side in about one second with 'ValueError: AZURE_AI_SERVICES_ENDPOINT (or AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT fallback) is not set'. The cosmos-rag server is healthy and its invocation counts stay balanced (34 Executing / 34 Executed), so this is not a server-side stall. The concurrent stage simply never surfaces the tool error and never completes the superstep.

So the defect is error propagation in the concurrent stage, not the tool failure itself: a failing tool should fail or degrade the bead, not wedge it. Reference runs complete bead 002 in about 1 minute.

Reproduce: ./scripts/run-prior-auth-local.sh (needs the compliance gate to pass first). Watch for 'Function name: hybrid_search' with no matching 'succeeded'.

Related: h3v. Configuring cosmos-rag would mask this locally but would not fix the underlying error handling. Note the demo resource only has text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims), while cosmos-rag's local.settings.json expects text-embedding-3-large (3072).

title: Compliance agent skips validation tools, gating valid requests
description:
In roughly 2 of 3 live prior-auth runs the compliance agent never calls validate_npi or validate_icd10 and then self-reports can_proceed=False, so the workflow PENDs a request whose codes are actually valid. One run called all three tools and passed the gate. This is LLM tool-selection nondeterminism, not a parsing defect: _check_compliance_gate correctly matched the model's own 'false' verdict.

Consider requiring tool use, or pre-validating codes deterministically before the agent runs and passing the results in as context.

UPDATE: partly explained. The one failing run observed called ONLY lookup_icd10, which at the time still had the undotted-query bug and returned 'Code not found' for a valid code. The agent's can_proceed=False was therefore a correct conclusion from wrong tool output, not pure nondeterminism. lookup_icd10 has since been fixed. Re-measure the gate pass rate before investing in prompt changes; the remaining question is only why tool selection varies.

title: cosmos-rag has no backing database in local runs
description:
COSMOS_DB_ENDPOINT defaults to https://localhost:8081 (the Cosmos emulator), which is not running. Audit writes therefore return HTTP 500 on every bead ('Failed to record audit event'), and hybrid_search cannot serve policy RAG. The workflow degrades rather than failing, but the audit trail is silently lost.

Note: an unreachable cosmos-rag is NOT merely degraded. MCPToolKit connects all servers up front, so if the server is down entirely the whole run aborts at 'async with toolkit'.

UPDATE: also unset locally are AZURE_AI_SERVICES_ENDPOINT and a usable embedding deployment, so hybrid_search raises before it ever reaches Cosmos. The demo AOAI resource has text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims), not the text-embedding-3-large (3072) configured in local.settings.json, so EMBEDDING_DEPLOYMENT_NAME and EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS both need changing alongside provisioning a database. This failure is what currently triggers h1g.

title: DevUI credential retry is dead code
description: In src/agents/framework_devui.py the try/except around DefaultAzureCredential() cannot fire: the constructor succeeds even with no credentials available (verified under env -i), because probing is deferred to get_token(), which is called outside the try. Preserved verbatim during the 1.8 migration because behavior preservation was a hard requirement. Either move the retry around the first token acquisition or remove it.
